create.title: Exact ordered odd-denominator resonance-cell decomposition
create.statement_tex: For odd d, chi_4(d)=-i e(d/4). With g_h(d)=hX/d+d/4 and R_h=hX/D^2, the exact increment is g_h(d+2)-g_h(d)=1/2-2hX/(d(d+2)). The bad absorbed-phase cells are dist(2hX/(d(d+2)),Z+1/2)<eta. For every accepted fixed-BV denominator profile, their count is O(min(D,eta D+R_h+1)); exact nonresonant summation by parts and optimization give |S_h(D;X)|<<_epsilon X^epsilon min(D,sqrt(hX/D)). Hence the actual Vaaler shell satisfies |B_(1,L)(D;X)|<<_epsilon X^epsilon min(D,sqrt(LX/D)). The bound is uniform at the hard top and closes no point of U_1 beyond the already accepted (1/2,0) and lower active edge.
create.next_action: Use the exact half-integral resonance law only as a reduction. Any improvement must retain cancellation between stationary cells or frequencies.

create.title: Capacity obstruction for separate M1 resonance-cell estimates
create.statement_tex: The natural half-width of a low-curvature resonance cell is rho_h=sqrt(D^3/(hX)), and there are asymp R_h=hX/D^2 possible cells, so separate absolute cell estimates cost R_h rho_h=sqrt(hX/D). The cells map under the odd-lattice B-process to odd dual frequencies q with d=2sqrt(hX/q), character chi_4(q), amplitude (hX)^(1/4)q^(-3/4), and phase e(sqrt(Xhq)). Thus separate cell counting is exactly the accepted V2/B-process loss, closes no point of U_1, and cannot be improved by generic two-variable curvature because sqrt(Xhq) has rank-one Hessian and is constant on product fibers. This does not obstruct signed cancellation between cells for the actual profile.
create.next_action: Reject cellwise-absolute or nonsingular-Hessian arguments; require the actual signed restricted convolution or cross-product phase cancellation.

create.title: Dual restricted-convolution estimate for M1 resonance cells
create.statement_tex: Let d_(h,q)=2sqrt(hX/q). Uniformly on U_1 and for the actual profiles, prove RCS: |sum_(h asymp L) u_(L,H)(h)(hX)^(1/4) sum_(q odd, d_(h,q) in supp(w_D))^* chi_4(q)q^(-3/4)w_D(d_(h,q))e(sqrt(Xhq))| <<_epsilon X^(1/4+epsilon). The star retains exact endpoint half weights. Grouping n=hq gives sum_n A^*_(D,L)(n;X)e(sqrt(Xn)), where A^* is the actual chi_4(q)-weighted restricted divisor convolution. Standard one-sided/interior B-process errors are target-sized, so RCS is equivalent to the unresolved M1 shell. Divisor multiplicity or product-fiber absolute values yield only sqrt(LX/D) and cannot prove RCS.
create.next_action: Simplify and attack the restricted convolution A^* before any product-fiber absolute value; test Mellin or Dirichlet-series separation with exact cutoffs and endpoint terms.

reject.reason: A single adjacent pair is small near integral alpha=2hX/(d(d+2)), not throughout the complement of the bad half-integer cells; nonresonant saving is a multi-term Kusmin--Landau statement.
A localized normalized-BV triangular profile can coherently attain the natural stationary size sqrt(D/R_h) on one cell.
Summing the natural cell sizes gives sqrt(hX/D), exactly the accepted V2/B-process loss, which closes no point of U_1.
The phase sqrt(Xhq) has determinant-zero Hessian and is constant on every product fiber hq=n.
The first differencing step removes the d-dependent character and gives only the classical untwisted reciprocal exponent, adding no point beyond the accepted menu.
Finite-field inverses, Kloosterman fractions, and separable multilinear monomials do not match the real one-variable reciprocal phase and actual coefficient hypotheses.
